# Why the review queue keeps growing

Every automated check we add creates work for a person downstream. Call it the
supervision paradox: the more review we automate, the more review we generate.

That feeds the acceleration trap, where shipping faster produces more of the
thing that slows you down. Underneath both sits ownership creep, which is what
happens when nobody is named on the rota.

None of that is scope creep in the ordinary sense. Scope creep has a budget
line and a change request behind it, and it shows up in planning.

The sunk cost fallacy explains some of the reluctance to delete the older
checks. A power vacuum after the reorg explains the rest, and the productivity
paradox is the economics term people usually reach for when they mean neither.
